pubspec.reason: the package name from pubspec.yaml is baked into the snapshot: it names the product, not the machine.

flutter.reason: the prebuilt Flutter engine is a third-party binary we do not compile; its strings are the framework's own and name no account.

dart.reason: the Dart VM inside that engine names itself; removing it would mean rebuilding Flutter from source.

cargo.reason: rustc records the source directory of every crate it compiles; the account prefix is remapped to /build by the 2026-11-02 fingerprint sweep, so what is left is the toolchain's own layout (.cargo\registry\src\...), which says which crates built the file, not who built it.

dart.reason: the package manifest names dartjni.dll among the files it lists, so the substring appears once: that is a shipped file name, not the Dart VM living in this binary.

flutter.reason: the manifest names every shipped file and 54 of them sit under data\flutter_assets\, with flutter_windows.dll making 55: these are the paths the start-up self-check hashes, not the toolchain that built the engine.

rustc.reason: the engine's panic, version and RUST_BACKTRACE strings name the compiler that produced them; none of them carries a path.

flutter.reason: the C++ runner calls the Flutter C API by name (DartProject, the view controller, the messenger).
